lines.text: Training one big AI model can take weeks, using hundreds of chips working at the same time.
lines.kicker: Training one AI model can take
lines.note: on hundreds of GPUs at once

lines.text: Those chips are GPUs. They are great at doing lots of maths at once, which is exactly what AI training needs.
lines.title: What's a GPU?

items.label: GPU
items.sub: does lots of maths at once

lines.text: They all work in step, like rowers in a boat. So one bad GPU can slow down, or stop, the whole job.
lines.title: One bad GPU slows everyone

lines.text: Netflix found a GPU can look healthy and still fail under real work. So it runs deeper checks, and a check that hangs counts as a failure.
lines.title: Looking healthy is not enough

lines.text: When a machine fails, repairs happen step by step. Stop giving it new work, move work off it, then reset or replace it.
lines.title: Netflix's automatic repair

lines.text: Training jobs also save progress often, called checkpoints. Like a save point in a video game, they restart from the last good spot.
lines.title: Checkpoints = save points

lines.text: The result: GPU machines are available over ninety nine point nine five percent of the time, and job success rose from about ninety eight to over ninety nine point five percent.
lines.title: The results

lines.text: The lesson: at big scale, hardware will fail. So build systems that notice problems and fix themselves.
lines.title: The big lesson

points.text: At big scale, hardware will fail
